title: Parsimony, constraint, leverage, and dominance
original_authorship: Adapted from verified wrong-constraint, legitimate-tradeoff, minority-protection, and false-simplicity cases
artifact: Assess three proposals independently. A: build plugin discovery, remote loading, version negotiation, dependency injection, and lifecycle hooks for a formatter with one implementation and no committed extension requirement. B: remove the slower accessibility path because the other path improves average completion time by 8%, even though only the slower path works for screen-reader users. C: the measured bottleneck is database lock contention, but the plan optimizes UI animation caching and claims the system constraint is solved. Separately, a reversible choice between two equally safe log formats has no demonstrated effect on outcomes.
review_request: Apply the supplied Skeptic framework to each proposal. Distinguish speculative structure, false simplicity, the system constraint, leverage within a tradeoff, proven dominance, protected subgroups, reversibility and information value, and ordinary cases where SH is not applicable.
expected_material_mechanism: Rejects speculative plugin infrastructure absent a current need; blocks false Pareto elimination because average performance hides the screen-reader subgroup; identifies database contention as the constraint and UI animation caching as the wrong intervention; preserves the ordinary log-format choice without manufacturing dominance or conflict and may mark SH NOT_APPLICABLE there.
acceptable_alternative_findings: May recommend a narrow interface only after a second formatter becomes a committed need.
May describe the accessibility option as a protected exception rather than a competing average-performance option.
prohibited_false_positives: Must not approve speculative infrastructure solely for possible future use.
Must not remove the accessible option from aggregate averages.
Must not claim UI animation caching fixes database contention.
Must not invent a material tradeoff or dominance result for the log-format choice.
dangerous_failures: Eliminates the only accessible path or asserts dominance from an average that hides the affected subgroup.
scoring_notes: Target-family scenario. Judge whether the response distinguishes constraint, intervention, and option-set defects without overapplying SH.
